title: Tutorials: making states in a component
goal: The Components track teaches versions with a button that has an on look and an off look, which undersells what somebody is really doing. A button has a resting look, a hovered look, a pressed look and a disabled look, and the reason to keep them under one name is so all four stay in step. Rewrite that guide to teach the four states people actually build, and to show how to see the button in each of them.
notes:
Asked for by the user on 2026-09-15: the button component tutorial's "2 states" thing should be "Making states in a component", covering "a button transitioning from rest, hovered, pressed, disabled, and how to preview the button in its different states".

The guide to rewrite is componentVersions in Sources/PhotonzCore/TutorialGuides.swift, id 'component-versions', currently titled "One name, two looks" with the summary "A button needs a disabled look too. Both live under one component." It teaches adding a second version under the Versions panel. So the mechanism it teaches is right; the story around it is thin.

WHAT THE APP ACTUALLY HAS, checked: components hold VERSIONS, a copy picks which version it shows, versions can be named, and the canvas says which version a copy is showing. There is no notion of an interaction state anywhere in the model - no hover, no pressed, no disabled - confirmed by grepping ComponentInstances and ComponentStyle. So states are a CONVENTION built on versions: you name four versions after the four states. That is exactly how designers work in other tools, and it is honest to teach it that way. Do not invent a states feature inside a tutorial.

That also means the previewing half needs care. 'See the button in each state' with what exists means placing four copies and pointing each at a different version, which is a real and useful thing to teach. If that turns out clumsy - if there is no quick way to flip one copy through its versions, or no way to see them together without arranging copies by hand - that is a genuine feature gap the user has just walked into from the other direction, and it belongs in a task of its own rather than being smoothed over in the guide's words. The acceptance list asks for exactly that.

Keep the existing guide's own rule, which is already written in its comment: it is called Versions because that is what the panel calls it, and a guide teaches what shipped rather than what the plan called it. If the guide's TITLE changes to talk about states, the steps must still name the Versions panel the person is looking at.
acceptance: The guide is called something that says what it is for, in the app's plain voice, rather than naming the mechanism
It teaches the four states a button really has: resting, hovered, pressed and disabled
It shows how to look at the button in each state, and the audit captures all four side by side as the guide leaves them
It says why they belong under one name: change the label or the corner and every state follows, so they cannot drift apart
It teaches what stays the same and what differs between states, so somebody does not redraw the button four times
It still teaches what actually shipped rather than what a plan called it, which is the rule the existing guide already follows
It is short enough to finish in the time its entry claims, measured rather than guessed
Every step points at something visible at that moment, and the guide behaves sensibly with the component flags off as well as on
If seeing all four states at once is awkward or impossible with what exists, that is written up as a finding and filed as its own task rather than worked around silently in the guide
Audit under queue/audits/ with the guide captured step by step, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Pre-build review. What the app really has: a component holds VARIANTS (the panel's word since 2026-09-15; 'Versions' is gone), each one a whole drawing on the canvas, and the variant PROPERTY can be renamed, with the panel's own help saying 'Call it State, or Type, or Size'. So states are not invented here: renaming the question to State is a shipped control, and it is what licenses the guide to say 'state' throughout instead of teaching a word the panel does not use.

Measured the budget before writing a word: the track's own tests cap a guide at 8 steps and 3 minutes, and TutorialLength.claimIsHonest holds the claim within a minute of the work. Eight steps is the whole budget, so every step had to earn itself. Cut from the plan: a step that presses Apply to Other Variants for real (needs a piece selected inside one drawing AND a difference to carry, or the row is dimmed reading 'Other Variants Already Match'), and a separate pick-a-copy step. Both fold into wording of steps that were already there.

Measured where four drawings actually land on the guide's sample (720x480, button 240x52 at 88,88): Default (88,88), Hover (352,88), Pressed (352,164), Disabled (352,240). All four fit inside the canvas and none overlap, so the guide really can leave all four states on screen together. They land as one drawing plus a column of three rather than a row of four, with the sample's two copies underneath the first: that is the honest shape of it and goes in the audit.
